module.purpose: Maintains an incremental per-page spatial index for locating shapes within bounds or near points. It tracks shape and binding history, expands affected records through structural relationships, and updates an R-tree only when derived page bounds change.
module.summary: This internal manager builds and maintains an R-tree-backed index of valid page-space shape bounds. It performs an initial bulk rebuild when dependencies reset or the active page changes, then incrementally processes shape and binding diffs. Dirty shapes are expanded through descendants, ancestors, and binding endpoints so derived bounds remain accurate while avoiding page-wide recomputation. Query methods force synchronization before returning unordered candidate IDs, and disposal releases the tree.
module.businessContext: Supports fast canvas hit testing and viewport culling in the editor. Incorrect indexing can omit visible or selectable shapes, while unnecessary rebuilds degrade editing performance.

Pending spatial-index removals and upserts are applied as one batched update.

units.name: getShapeIdsInsideBounds
units.source:
a: Box | undefined,
		b: SpatialElement | undefined
	): boolean {
		if (!a && !b) return true
		if (!a || !b) return false
		return a.minX === b.minX && a.minY === b.minY && a.maxX === b.maxX && a.maxY === b.maxY
	}

	/**
	 * Get shape IDs within the given bounds.
	 * Optimized for viewport culling queries.
	 *
	 * Note: Results are unordered. If you need z-order, combine with sorted shapes:
	 * ```ts
	 * const candidates = editor.spatialIndex.getShapeIdsInsideBounds(bounds)
	 * const sorted = editor.getCurrentPageShapesSorted().filter(s => candidates.has(s.id))
	 * ```
	 *
	 * @param bounds - The bounds to search within

detail.name: getShapeIdsInsideBounds
preconditions: bounds is a valid Box with minX, minY, maxX, and maxY coordinates.
postconditions: Returns a Set containing each matching shape ID at most once.
The result contains no ordering guarantee.
invariants: The input bounds and indexed shape state are not mutated.
The returned collection is a set of shape IDs rather than shape objects.
edgeCases: If no indexed spatial elements match the bounds, returns an empty Set.
Results may be returned in any order.
detail.summary: Returns the IDs of shapes whose spatial bounds are found within or overlapping the supplied query bounds. Results are returned as an unordered set suitable for viewport-culling candidate selection.

units.name: getShapeIdsAtPoint
units.source:
*
	 * @public
	 */
	getShapeIdsInsideBounds(bounds: Box): Set<TLShapeId> {
		this.spatialIndexComputed.get()
		return this.rbush.search(bounds)
	}

	/**
	 * Get shape IDs at a point (with optional margin).
	 * Creates a small bounding box around the point and searches the spatial index.
	 *
	 * Note: Results are unordered. If you need z-order, combine with sorted shapes:
	 * ```ts
	 * const candidates = editor.spatialIndex.getShapeIdsAtPoint(point, margin)
	 * const sorted = editor.getCurrentPageShapesSorted().filter(s => candidates.has(s.id))
	 * ```
	 *
	 * @param point - The point to search at
	 * @param margin - The margin around the point to search (default: 0)
	 * @returns Unordered set of shape IDs that could potentially contain the point

detail.name: getShapeIdsAtPoint
preconditions: point provides numeric x and y coordinates.
The spatial index can be initialized or synchronized before searching.
postconditions: Returns a Set<TLShapeId> containing the spatial-index candidates intersecting the point search area.
The returned set is not ordered by z-order or document order.
invariants: The method performs candidate lookup through the spatial index rather than guaranteeing exact geometric point containment.
A positive margin expands the search area equally in both coordinate dimensions.
edgeCases: With the default margin of 0, the search area is centered on the point without intentional expansion.
With a positive margin, shapes intersecting the expanded area may be included even when they do not contain the exact point.
Results are unordered and may require separate shape-order sorting when z-order is needed.
detail.summary: Returns an unordered set of shape IDs whose spatial-indexed bounds may contain the specified point. An optional margin expands the point into a search area before querying the spatial index.

specLiterals.role: Default margin when no expansion is requested.

specTests.when: getShapeIdsAtPoint(point) is called with the default margin
specTests.then: It returns an unordered Set containing the IDs of spatial-index candidates intersecting the point search area.
It searches the area expanded by the margin in both x and y directions and may return candidates that do not contain the exact point.
